inert_witness.text:
# Contracts
## Payload
```json
"function guest(){return 19;/* ROOT_PAYLOAD_R19 */}"
```
## Mirror
```ts public-api
export type Mirror = "function guest(){return 19;/* ROOT_PAYLOAD_R19 */}";
```
inert_witness.setup: Textual counterexample only. Use a pinned synthetic source with the owner-map structure shown at tests:19-28,135-175; no fixture or code was executed.

derivation: collectReferenceCatalog selects docs/tool-catalog.md (271-274,1697-1708); extractDocument prepasses all fences before emitting (1347-1402).

The JSON prepass calls jsonPayloadLiterals(JSON.parse(content), undefined, declaration, sharedMap) at 1359-1365. At 1197-1204 a primitive string in declaration role is not payload, so the full guest string is never indexed. There are no JSON members to take another branch.

Projection of that same root string reaches 1239-1263: field is undefined and role is declaration, so none of the vocabulary exemptions matches. The document-json shape is explicitly UNKNOWN with the string digest/length.
The second fence contains only a literal type alias. indexRuntimeLiterals skips type syntax (741-747); printed finds no indexed collision at 558-581 and prints the entire quoted literal at 583-586.

The raw alias symbol Contracts/Mirror/Mirror passes identityVocabulary. emitFor at 1615-1641 neither traverses nor sanitizes strings in shape. The document-type entry is STATIC and contains the complete previously unclassified JSON payload as a declared type.

This is a same-physical-source unresolved payload collision, not cross-file resolution or an objection to a declaration-only program-shaped selector. Removing the JSON fence restores the required frozen-B positive case.

findings.title: Built-in JSON schema type strings bypass a known same-source executable-payload collision
frozen_rules: C actual program source opaque in every output representation

inert_witness.setup: Inert text only. Worker is present as source syntax, never constructed. The complete JavaScript guest program is the four-byte literal null.

derivation: The TypeScript prepass visits the actual Worker argument, indexing hash(null) at 735-770. The mirrored literal type is therefore UNKNOWN with that digest and length through printed at 558-581.
The document-json object receives the same shared payloadLiterals map at 1465-1470. Its type field enters vocabulary role through jsonChildRole (1180-1181).

At 1241-1251, role is not payload and null is in the hardcoded type list. Unlike the name/required and $ref branches at 1252-1257, this branch never tests payloadLiterals.has(hash(value)); it returns the exact string null at 1259.

The JSON entry shape is only {type:"null"}; hasUnknown is false, so emitFor marks that entry STATIC. The program remains opaque in the mirrored TypeScript type but appears verbatim in the JSON type representation.

This is not the JSON primitive null, a filename, dynamic evaluation, or a cross-file inference. It is the exact string supplied as guest source and reused as a literal schema constraint in one physical document.

findings.title: Mermaid node IDs and simple edges copy an indexed guest program verbatim
frozen_rules: C actual program source opaque in every output representation

inert_witness.text:
# Contracts
## Runtime
```ts public-api
export type Mirror = "debugger";
new Worker("debugger", { eval: true });
```
## Graph
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  debugger["node"]
  sink["target"]
  debugger --> sink
```
inert_witness.setup: Inert text only. debugger is a complete eight-byte JavaScript program; the Worker source is never run.

derivation: The shared Markdown prepass indexes the Worker argument debugger through 1366-1373 and 735-770. printed correctly makes the literal type Mirror UNKNOWN with its hash/length.
The Mermaid node regex at 1499 matches debugger["node"]. Line 1501 assigns match[1] directly to nodes[0].id. The projection at 1502 handles the label only, and receives no shared collision map.
The line "  debugger --> sink" passes both edge regular expressions at 1506 and 1508. Line 1509 emits row.trim(), exactly "debugger --> sink", with the same guest source bytes retained.

The add wrapper at 1403-1410 examines the symbol Contracts/Graph, not nested nodes or edges. That symbol contains no payload; emitFor retains the shape unchanged. Graph semantics is UNKNOWN, but this status does not remove the raw bytes.
No file resolution, semantic graph interpretation or whole-program analysis is needed to derive these outputs. The witness is intentionally restricted to the grammar the actual regex accepts.

findings.title: Genuine export module selectors with spaces or punctuation lose their exact declaration spelling
frozen_rules: B genuine declared selectors preserve exact spelling regardless of lexical program appearance
A/B exact metadata can coexist with opaque identity

inert_witness.setup: Inert TypeScript export syntax only; no module loading or existence/resolution claim. Use the synthetic package/owner structure in the sealed tests.

derivation: indexRuntimeLiterals skips ExportDeclaration at 743-747. There is no runtime payload anywhere in this source, so the moduleSpecifier is a genuine static declaration selector with no unresolved collision.

The export branch calls nodeName(node.moduleSpecifier) at 944-945 instead of declarationName. At 590-593 the spaces and question/exclamation punctuation fail identityVocabulary and produce an opaque UNKNOWN containing only digest/length.

The named export receives symbol Config and shape {from:opaque, name:"Config", type_only:false} at 949-958. declared_name is conditional on item.name being a string, which it is not in this witness, and would describe the exported name rather than the module locator anyway.

No separate exact module selector is retained in shape or symbol. emitFor keeps the Config identity and only the digest of the module locator. Authenticated source path provenance remains correct; that does not preserve the separate selector contract.

This finding requires no cross-file resolution or executable interpretation of the selector. It concerns only inert exact spelling, already preserved for ambient module context at 826-829 and by declarationName when used.
